# Community Management and Contribution Workflows

A Linux distribution is more than compiled code; it is a collaborative community of software maintainers, packagers, documenters, and bug triagers. Without clear governance and contribution pipelines, distributions collapse under maintenance fatigue.

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|                   Distro Governance Layers                |
|                                                           |
| 1. Core Technical Steering Committee (TSC / Release Team) |
|    - Final decision on architecture, tools, and releases  |
|                                                           |
| 2. Package Maintainers (Direct repository commit rights)  |
|    - Responsible for specific packages (e.g. kernel, X11) |
|                                                           |
| 3. Contributors & Packagers                               |
|    - Submit recipe PRs / patches via Git Forge            |
|                                                           |
| 4. Community Testers & Bug Hunters                        |
|    - Test staging repositories and submit bug reports     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Designing the Git Recipe Monorepo

For small to medium distributions, managing thousands of individual git repositories (one per package) creates massive administrative overhead.

A cleaner, modern approach is a **single recipe monorepo** (similar to Void Linux's `void-packages` or Alpine's `aports`):

```text
byol-packages/
├── .github/workflows/
│   └── build-and-test.yml
├── common/
│   ├── build-helper.sh
│   └── makepkg.conf
└── packages/
    ├── bash/
    │   ├── BYOLBUILD
    │   └── 0001-fix-path.patch
    ├── curl/
    │   └── BYOLBUILD
    └── linux/
        ├── BYOLBUILD
        └── config-x86_64
```

### Advantages of the Monorepo:
1. **Atomic PRs:** A contributor proposing a shared library upgrade (e.g., updating `zlib`) can update the library recipe *and* all downstream rebuilt packages in a single pull request.
2. **Unified Issue Tracking:** Users file bug reports against a single centralized repository.
3. **Automated CI Linting:** A GitHub Actions or Forgejo runner can run `shellcheck`, parse `BYOLBUILD` syntax, and execute test builds on every incoming PR.
